title: Leveraging large language models for BIM-based automated compliance checking
inputData: 建筑规范文本 + BIM模型数据 + 预定义数据提取/检查工具
contribution: 提出LLM中心的端到端BIM自动合规检查框架，使模型直接解释规范、选择并调用BIM数据提取工具、执行规则检查并生成带推理依据的合规报告，从而绕过传统ACC中人工规则数字化的主要瓶颈。
abstract: Automated compliance checking in AECO is constrained by the effort required to manually digitize regulatory rules. Using design science research, this study develops an LLM-centric artifact that directly interprets building regulations, prepares BIM data, executes compliance checks, and generates detailed reports. The artifact achieves 97% F1 for rule classification, 100% F1 for dependency identification, correctly selects BIM data-extraction tools in 97% of cases, and reaches 97.7% accuracy in rule execution. The final reports include the LLM's reasoning, demonstrating a holistic alternative to traditional rule-digitization pipelines.
methodology: The artifact organizes compliance checking as a multi-stage LLM-driven workflow. Regulatory clauses are first interpreted to determine rule type and dependencies. For requirements that need model information, the LLM identifies the appropriate pre-written BIM data-extraction functions and orchestrates their use to obtain task-relevant structured model data. The resulting values are evaluated against the interpreted regulation, after which the system synthesizes the checking result and supporting reasoning into a detailed compliance report. The study evaluates rule interpretation, tool selection/model preparation, rule execution, and reporting as separate stages of the end-to-end artifact.
results: Rule interpretation achieved 97% F1 for classification and 100% F1 for dependency identification. During BIM model preparation, the artifact selected the correct data-extraction tool in 97% of evaluated cases. Rule execution reached 97.7% accuracy and significantly outperformed a naive baseline. The reporting stage produced detailed compliance reports containing the model's reasoning, showing that the structured multi-stage workflow can support end-to-end BIM-based regulatory checking.
inputDataEn: Building regulations plus BIM model data and predefined extraction/checking tools
operationEvidence: The LLM maps regulatory requirements to relevant BIM extraction functions, invokes those tools and executes checks on structured model data, determines compliance, and generates a detailed compliance report with supporting reasoning.
